atlas-om.0088: Starting work, a trial day or an internship after a visa-free entry: the library cites a fine of OMR 1,000 to 2,000, 10 days to 1 month in prison, expulsion and a GCC blacklist.
atlas-om.0089: Planning a post-study job search in the country: the library finds no job-seeker visa and about 30 days of grace, with an overstay fine of OMR 10 a day.
atlas-om.0090: Arriving without the degree equivalency or, in engineering, logistics or accounting, the pre-arrival skills-unit assessment: entry permits follow the work practice licence.
atlas-om.0091: Applying to the Omani-only programmes (PDO, OQ, Oman Airports) as a foreign graduate.
atlas-om.0092: KPMG Middle East’s online assessments include English, and the central bank’s circular asks banks to reach Omanisation above 90%, so Arabic is likely the working language of most bank teams. No source measured the level employers ask.
atlas-om.0093: English is standard for multinational firms and Arabic is often required for government and local companies, according to a CV guide; the labour contract must be in Arabic.
atlas-om.0094: Omanis made up 90.2% of government employment in 2025 and a CV guide says Arabic is often required for government employers; we found no page stating an Arabic level.
atlas-om.0095: Programmers and computer engineers are closed to new expatriate hires from 1 January 2026, and we found no page testing English or Arabic for graduates in software, data or cybersecurity. This is our reading.
atlas-om.0096: The job-seeker rate was 2.4% in June 2026 (6.4% for women, 1.3% for men) and 13.2% for ages 15 to 24; among holders of a bachelor’s degree it was 12.4% for women and 1.3% for men, and 0.5% for master’s and doctoral holders. These are Omani-population figures: we found no graduate-specific figure for expatriates, and no return-offer or time-to-first-job figure.
atlas-om.0097: In the Ministry of Higher Education’s Employer Survey 2025 of 1,083 private organisations, 68% had hired Omani graduates, 47% had hired graduates with no work experience, 38% found it hard to recruit them for lack of practical experience and 76% were satisfied with their performance.
atlas-om.0098: The university, accredited by the higher-education ministry, sponsors the visa; you need an unconditional offer, apostilled certificates with an equivalency certificate, and a medical on arrival.
atlas-om.0099: Students may not work at all, not even part time; only unpaid required placements with the university’s approval.
atlas-om.0100: visa 30 OMR; card 5 OMR a year; medical 30 OMR
atlas-om.0102: There is no company internship visa: an unpaid internship arranged privately is illegal work. A training visa can be sponsored only by an Omani university or accredited training institution; it pays an allowance, not a wage, and cannot become a work visa inside the country.
atlas-om.0103: There is no job-search permit: graduates have about 30 days to leave or be hired, and Omanisation keeps most entry-level roles for Omanis.
atlas-om.0105: The employer obtains labour clearance and the employment visa before you travel; after arrival come the medical, fingerprints and the resident card. The employer pays all fees.
atlas-om.0106: Over 207 occupations are reserved for Omanis, including marketing, sales, HR and, since January 2026, programmers and computer engineers. Engineers and doctors also need professional licensing.
atlas-om.0110: Residence without a sponsor: ten years for an investment of 500,000 OMR (or a 200,000 OMR property in tourist complexes), five years for 250,000 OMR.
atlas-om.0112: Fieldwork, sampling or interviews as a tourist are forbidden: a host institution requests a research visa and the ministry issues a researcher facilitation letter.
atlas-om.0113: PhD students hold a student visa; there is no income tax, and the scholarship needs no labour permit.
atlas-om.0114: Oman has no working-holiday agreements; casual work on a tourist visa leads to detention, expulsion and a Gulf-wide ban.
atlas-om.0115: 14 days visa-free, or a tourist eVisa
atlas-om.0116: Citizens of 103 countries, the EU included, enter free for 14 days with a return ticket, hotel booking and health insurance; before day 14 you can switch to a 30-day tourist visa. Since October 2023 no visit visa can become a work visa inside Oman.
atlas-om.0118: A tourist visa cannot be turned into a work visa inside Oman: your employer gets the employment visa online, and you travel with a passport valid more than 6 months and the printed visa.
atlas-om.0119: Do not pack medicines with benzodiazepines, opioids such as codeine or tramadol, ADHD stimulants or CBD without prior approval from the Ministry of Health: it can mean arrest for drug trafficking at Muscat airport.
atlas-om.0120: Register your lease on the Muscat Municipality’s Ejar portal, paying the 3% municipal fee; electricity and water are then transferred to that contract.
atlas-om.0121: Once declared fit, give fingerprints and a photo at the police Civil Status directorate and receive the resident card on the spot (10 OMR for 2 years). You may not work before the card is issued and the contract registered with the Ministry of Labour.
atlas-om.0122: Book the medical fitness check through a Sanad centre (30 OMR): blood tests for HIV, hepatitis B and C and syphilis, and a tuberculosis test. An unfit result means the visa is cancelled and you are expelled, with no appeal.
atlas-om.0123: Buy an Omani SIM in your passport name, needed for digital identity; then open an account (Bank Muscat, NBO, Sohar International) with your resident card, passport and the employer’s salary transfer letter, linked to the Wages Protection System.
atlas-om.0124: Overstaying costs 10 OMR a day on a visit visa and 20 OMR a day from 30 days after a resident card expires, with no cap: you cannot leave until you pay.
atlas-om.0125: Italians can convert their driving licence without a test, with an eye check and a 20 OMR fee.
atlas-om.0126: Overstay costs 10 OMR a day with no cap, and you cannot board until it is paid.
atlas-om.0127: Working before the resident card is issued and the contract registered is illegal work, punished with jail, fines and a Gulf-wide ban.
atlas-om.0128: A positive test for HIV, hepatitis B or C, syphilis or TB in the arrival medical means expulsion, with no appeal.
atlas-om.0129: Benzodiazepines, codeine, tramadol, ADHD stimulants or CBD without Health Ministry approval lead to arrest at customs.
atlas-om.0130: Bringing family normally needs 600 OMR a month; whether the police accept 300 OMR for academics, doctors and engineers is case by case.
atlas-om.0131: Ministries still often ask for foreign-ministry attestation of documents despite the apostille.
atlas-om.0132: Whether business and management graduates will also need source verification of degrees.
